lines.text: Sam laces his boots extra tight for the cold.
One hour in, his toes are numb.
Tight boots squeeze the blood flow that keeps feet warm,
and his socks are damp with sweat.
Here's the fix. Leave room to wiggle your toes.
Wear merino socks that stay warm when they get damp,
and pack a dry spare pair for lunch.
Sam swaps socks on a rock, and his feet start to warm.
Save this before your next cold hike.
